## 1.2 Load data and process

### 1.2.1 Load Data from 00
```{r}
library(janitor)

# Load the saved Rds file
loaded_objects <- readRDS("00data_Pediatric.rds")

# Assign back the objects to the environment, if needed
list2env(loaded_objects, .GlobalEnv)

ps_sglom <- tax_glom(ps_fs, taxrank = "Species", NArm = TRUE)

ps_sglom <- psmelt(ps_sglom)
 
ps_sglom_df <- ps_sglom %>%
    dplyr::select(c("Sample", "Abundance", "Species")) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = "Species", values_from = "Abundance") %>% t() %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  row_to_names(row_number = 1) %>%
  mutate_all(., function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))
```


```{r}
otu_table <- ps_fs@otu_table %>% as.matrix() %>% as.data.frame()

mark_overlapping_asvs <- function(otu_table) {
  # Ensure ASV IDs are row names
  if (!"ASV0001" %in% rownames(otu_table)) {
    stop("ASV IDs must be row names")
  }
  
  # Get sample names
  sample_names <- colnames(otu_table)
  
  # Identify paired sample IDs (e.g., "100" from "100-A" and "100-P")
  paired_ids <- unique(gsub("(-A)|(-P)", "", sample_names))
  
  # Create a new data frame to store overlap (same dimensions as original)
  overlap_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(otu_table), ncol = length(paired_ids))
  rownames(overlap_matrix) <- rownames(otu_table)
  colnames(overlap_matrix) <- paste0(paired_ids, "_overlap")

  for (id in paired_ids) {
    a_sample <- paste0(id, "-A")
    p_sample <- paste0(id, "-P")

    if (a_sample %in% sample_names && p_sample %in% sample_names) {
      # Check where ASVs are present in both A and P (non-zero in both)
      overlap_matrix[, paste0(id, "_overlap")] <- as.integer(
        otu_table[, a_sample] > 0 & otu_table[, p_sample] > 0
      )
    } else {
      warning(paste("Missing pair for ID:", id))
    }
  }
  # Convert to data frame and add sum column
  overlap_df <- as.data.frame(overlap_matrix)
  overlap_df$sum_overlap <- rowSums(overlap_df)  
  overlap_df <- overlap_df %>% rownames_to_column(var="ASV") %>% arrange(dplyr::desc(sum_overlap)) %>% column_to_rownames(var="ASV")

  return(overlap_df)
}

overlap_df <- mark_overlapping_asvs(otu_table) %>% filter(sum_overlap > 12 )
print(overlap_df)

# Get top 10 ASV names from the OTU table
top_asvs <- rownames(overlap_df)

# Extract the tax_table (convert to data.frame for easier handling)
tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_fs))

# Make sure ASV names match
if (!all(top_asvs %in% rownames(tax_df))) {
  stop("Some ASVs in the OTU table are not found in the phyloseq tax_table.")
}

# Subset to just the top ASVs and select Genus and Species
top_asv_tax <- tax_df[top_asvs, c("Genus", "Species")]

# Optional: Add ASV as a column (not just rownames)
top_asv_tax$ASV <- rownames(top_asv_tax)
top_asv_tax <- top_asv_tax[, c("ASV", "Genus", "Species")]

# View result
top_overlap_info <- overlap_df %>%
  rownames_to_column("ASV") %>%
  filter(ASV %in% top_asvs) %>%
  dplyr::select(ASV, sum_overlap)

top_combined <- dplyr::left_join(top_asv_tax, top_overlap_info, by = "ASV")

print(top_combined)
```

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=1.5}
# Transform to relative abundance
ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_fs, function(x) x / sum(x))

# Melt into long format
ps_df <- psmelt(ps_rel)

# Filter for only the target ASVs
ps_df_filtered <- ps_df %>% 
  filter(OTU %in% top_combined$ASV)

# Extract sample ID (remove -A / -P) to group by sample pairs
ps_df_filtered <- ps_df_filtered %>%
  mutate(SamplePair = gsub("(-A)|(-P)", "", Sample),
         Compartment = ifelse(grepl("-A", Sample), "Abscess", "Plaque"))

# Pivot wider to get one row per ASV per sample pair, with separate Abscess and Plaque columns
ps_wide <- ps_df_filtered %>%
  select(OTU, SamplePair, Compartment, Abundance) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Compartment, values_from = Abundance) %>%
  mutate(ratio = Plaque / Abscess,
         log2_ratio = log2(ratio))%>%
  mutate(direction = case_when(
    is.infinite(log2_ratio) | is.nan(log2_ratio) ~ 0,
    log2_ratio > 0 ~ 1,
    log2_ratio < 0 ~ -1,
    TRUE ~ 0  # fallback for log2_ratio == 0
  ))

# Plot heatmap
ggplot(ps_wide, aes(x = SamplePair, y = OTU, fill = direction)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#4C2C69", high = "#ABFAA9", mid = "white", 
                       midpoint = 0, na.value = "grey90",
                       name = "log2(Abscess / Plaque)") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "ASV Enrichment: Plaque vs. Abscess",
       x = "Sample Pair",
       y = "") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```
